classification.difficultyReason: Directly compare the supplied curves' horizontal spreads and centres on identical scales.

content.prompt: The normal curves below are drawn with the same scale on each horizontal axis and the same scale on each vertical axis. Which distribution has the:

spec.description: Three unshaded normal curves in left-to-right order A, B, C, using identical axis units. Each panel has positive-direction axis arrowheads, labels f and x, and six equally spaced unnumbered horizontal-axis ticks. Decorative orange curves and teal panel labels are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: A is broadest and lowest, centred at its third tick. B has intermediate spread and height, centred at its fourth tick. C is narrowest and tallest, centred halfway between its second and third ticks. Schematic normal-density curves preserve these comparisons; no numerical parameters are student givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied graphs remain visible in the student edition; no answers appear in the diagrams.

answer.worked: A has the greatest horizontal spread, so it has the largest standard deviation.
C has the least horizontal spread, so it has the smallest standard deviation.
B is centred furthest to the right on the common horizontal scale, so it has the largest mean.
C is centred furthest to the left on the common horizontal scale, so it has the smallest mean.
